title: Humour and resilience
paragraphs: Sometimes life doesn’t seem to play fair. It blindsides you at the most inopportune moments, and even if we can learn to grin and bear the ups and downs, they can take their toll on our psyche. So rather than suffer in silence or let these things get you down, maybe there is another way: what if humour can help you get through the dark times?

According to author and clinician Kristen Lee: “Laughter and tears are both therapeutic – we need both to process such hard times.” But how can we find the tough things that happen funny? Our lives are really serious, often filled with mundane and repetitive activities, whether it’s arbitrary bill paying or fighting for a seat on your commute, we need to make time for fun and play – enjoy the little things. Why not make funny noises to remind you to stop taking things seriously, or learn some silly jokes, just to tell when times get hard? They could make you or other people around you laugh!

When a hurdle pops up in life, it’s easy to get bogged down – but the way we recount events can impact on our resilience. Rather than see the negatives, look for the ironic moments and tell people about them! Why not write parodies in your spare time about events that take place to help you compartmentalise? Script what happened as if it was happening to a character rather than yourself. We all know that some things in life aren’t fair. But take those events and send them up a bit in your scripts! Sometimes life needs a bit of a roasting to get your thoughts in order, and embracing your comedic side, seeing life’s difficult moments as obstacles that can be made fun of rather than overwhelm you, may help you get through them more easily. And who knows, you may just discover a talent for writing at the end of it.

vocabulary.entry: blindside /ˈblaɪndsaɪd/ v. 出其不意地攻击；使措手不及
vocabulary.example: The sudden resignation of the CEO blindsided the entire company.
vocabulary.translation: 首席执行官的突然辞职让整个公司都措手不及。

vocabulary.entry: inopportune /ɪnˈɒpətjuːn/ adj. 不合时宜的；时机不当的
vocabulary.example: The phone call came at an inopportune moment during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 电话在会议开到一半的尴尬时刻打了进来。

vocabulary.entry: psyche /ˈsaɪki/ n. 心理；精神
vocabulary.example: The traumatic experience left a deep mark on her psyche.
vocabulary.translation: 这次创伤性经历在她的心理上留下了深深的烙印。

vocabulary.entry: therapeutic /ˌθerəˈpjuːtɪk/ adj. 治疗的；具有治愈作用的
vocabulary.example: Gardening can be a therapeutic activity for people with anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 园艺对焦虑人群来说是一项具有治愈作用的活动。

vocabulary.entry: mundane /ˈmʌndeɪn/ adj. 单调的；平淡无奇的
vocabulary.example: She was tired of the mundane routine of her office job.
vocabulary.translation: 她厌倦了办公室工作的单调日常。

vocabulary.entry: arbitrary /ˈɑːbɪtrəri/ adj. 任意的；随心所欲的
vocabulary.example: The decision to increase prices seemed arbitrary and unfair.
vocabulary.translation: 涨价的决定看起来既随意又不公平。

vocabulary.entry: commute /kəˈmjuːt/ n. 通勤路程；上下班往返
vocabulary.example: Her daily commute takes about 45 minutes by train.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天坐火车通勤大约需要45分钟。

vocabulary.entry: hurdle /ˈhɜːdl/ n. 障碍；难关
vocabulary.example: Lack of funding is the main hurdle for the new project.
vocabulary.translation: 资金短缺是这个新项目的主要障碍。

vocabulary.entry: bog down /bɒɡ daʊn/ v. 使陷入困境；停滞不前
vocabulary.example: The negotiations were bogged down by technical details.
vocabulary.translation: 谈判因技术细节问题陷入了僵局。

vocabulary.entry: recount /rɪˈkaʊnt/ v. 讲述；叙述
vocabulary.example: She recounted her adventure in the jungle to her eager listeners.
vocabulary.translation: 她向热切的听众讲述了自己在丛林中的冒险经历。

vocabulary.entry: resilience /rɪˈzɪliəns/ n. 韧性；适应力
vocabulary.example: Children often show remarkable resilience after facing difficulties.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们在遭遇困境后往往会表现出惊人的韧性。

vocabulary.entry: ironic /aɪˈrɒnɪk/ adj. 讽刺的；具有讽刺意味的
vocabulary.example: It's ironic that the firefighter's house burned down last night.
vocabulary.translation: 消防员的房子昨晚被烧毁了，这真是件极具讽刺意味的事。

vocabulary.entry: parody /ˈpærədi/ n. 戏仿作品；滑稽模仿之作
vocabulary.example: The film is a hilarious parody of classic spy movies.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影是对经典间谍片的滑稽戏仿，十分搞笑。

vocabulary.entry: compartmentalise /ˌkɒmpɑːtˈmentəlaɪz/ v. 划分；分类处理
vocabulary.example: She learned to compartmentalise her work and personal life to reduce stress.
vocabulary.translation: 她学会了划分工作和个人生活，以减轻压力。

vocabulary.entry: script /skrɪpt/ v. 写剧本；编剧本
vocabulary.example: The writer was hired to script a new drama series for the TV channel.
vocabulary.translation: 这位作家受聘为电视台编写一部新的电视剧剧本。

vocabulary.entry: send up /send ʌp/ v. 嘲讽；挖苦
vocabulary.example: The comedian sent up the politician's mannerisms in his act.
vocabulary.translation: 这位喜剧演员在表演中嘲讽了那位政客的举止。

vocabulary.entry: roast /rəʊst/ n. 吐槽；调侃
vocabulary.example: The celebrity agreed to attend the charity roast for a good cause.
vocabulary.translation: 这位名人同意出席这场慈善吐槽大会，支持公益事业。

vocabulary.entry: comedic /kəˈmiːdɪk/ adj. 喜剧的；滑稽的
vocabulary.example: The actor's comedic timing is perfect, making every joke land.
vocabulary.translation: 这位演员的喜剧节奏把握得恰到好处，每个笑话都能引人发笑。

vocabulary.entry: obstacle /ˈɒbstəkl/ n. 障碍；阻碍
vocabulary.example: Poor eyesight was never an obstacle to her passion for reading.
vocabulary.translation: 视力不佳从未成为她热爱阅读的阻碍。

vocabulary.entry: overwhelm /ˌəʊvəˈwelm/ v. 压倒；使不知所措
vocabulary.example: She was overwhelmed by the amount of work she had to do.
vocabulary.translation: 堆积如山的工作让她感到手足无措。

vocabulary.entry: talent /ˈtælənt/ n. 天赋；才能
vocabulary.example: He has a natural talent for playing the piano.
vocabulary.translation: 他天生就有弹钢琴的天赋。

vocabulary.entry: toll /təʊl/ n. （身心的）损耗；代价
vocabulary.example: Years of hard work took a toll on his health.
vocabulary.translation: 多年的辛勤工作损害了他的健康。

vocabulary.entry: grin and bear /ɡrɪn ənd beə/ v. 默默忍受；逆来顺受
vocabulary.example: He had to grin and bear the unfair criticism from his boss.
vocabulary.translation: 他不得不默默忍受老板不公正的批评。

vocabulary.entry: suffer in silence /ˈsʌfə ɪn ˈsaɪləns/ v. 默默忍受痛苦
vocabulary.example: She suffered in silence for years before seeking help for her depression.
vocabulary.translation: 她默默忍受了多年抑郁的痛苦，才去寻求帮助。

vocabulary.entry: get down /ɡet daʊn/ v. 使沮丧；使情绪低落
vocabulary.example: Don't let the bad news get you down; things will get better.
vocabulary.translation: 别让坏消息影响你的心情，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.english: Sometimes life doesn’t seem to play fair.
sentences.chinese: 有时候生活似乎并不公平。

sentences.english: It blindsides you at the most inopportune moments, and even if we can learn to grin and bear the ups and downs, they can take their toll on our psyche.
sentences.chinese: 它总在最不合时宜的时刻出其不意地打击我们，即便我们能学默默承受人生的起起落落，这些经历也会对我们的心理造成伤害。

sentences.english: So rather than suffer in silence or let these things get you down, maybe there is another way: what if humour can help you get through the dark times?
sentences.chinese: 所以，与其默默承受痛苦，或是任由这些事情击垮自己，或许还有另一种办法：用幽默来帮你度过低谷期会怎么样呢？

sentences.english: According to author and clinician Kristen Lee: “Laughter and tears are both therapeutic – we need both to process such hard times.”
sentences.chinese: 作家兼临床医师克里斯汀·李表示：“欢笑与泪水都具有治愈功能——面对艰难时刻，我们需要二者兼备才能消化那些情绪。”

sentences.english: But how can we find the tough things that happen funny?
sentences.chinese: 但我们该如何从糟糕的事情中找到笑点呢？

sentences.english: Our lives are really serious, often filled with mundane and repetitive activities, whether it’s arbitrary bill paying or fighting for a seat on your commute, we need to make time for fun and play – enjoy the little things.
sentences.chinese: 生活本就十分严肃，还常常充斥着单调重复的琐事，无论是毫无理由地付账单，还是通勤时抢座位，我们都需要挤出时间自娱自乐——享受生活中的小确幸。

sentences.english: Why not make funny noises to remind you to stop taking things seriously, or learn some silly jokes, just to tell when times get hard?
sentences.chinese: 不妨试着弄出些搞怪的声响来提醒自己别把一切都看得太严肃，或者学几个无聊的笑话，专门在境遇不顺的时候讲出来。

sentences.english: They could make you or other people around you laugh!
sentences.chinese: 这些小举动说不定能让你自己，或是身边的人开怀一笑！

sentences.english: When a hurdle pops up in life, it’s easy to get bogged down – but the way we recount events can impact on our resilience.
sentences.chinese: 当生活中出现难关时，人很容易陷入困顿——但我们讲述经历的方式，会影响自身的心理韧性。

sentences.english: Rather than see the negatives, look for the ironic moments and tell people about them!
sentences.chinese: 与其只盯着消极的一面，不如去发掘那些充满讽刺意味的瞬间，讲给别人听！

sentences.english: Why not write parodies in your spare time about events that take place to help you compartmentalise?
sentences.chinese: 闲暇时，何不为发生过的事情写一些戏仿作品，帮助自己梳理情绪呢？

sentences.english: Script what happened as if it was happening to a character rather than yourself.
sentences.chinese: 把所经历的事情写成剧本，就当这些事发生在某个角色身上，而非你自己。

sentences.english: We all know that some things in life aren’t fair.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道，生活中有些事本就不公平。

sentences.english: But take those events and send them up a bit in your scripts!
sentences.chinese: 但不妨把这些事写进剧本里调侃一番！

sentences.english: Sometimes life needs a bit of a roasting to get your thoughts in order, and embracing your comedic side, seeing life’s difficult moments as obstacles that can be made fun of rather than overwhelm you, may help you get through them more easily.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，生活需要被“吐槽”一番，才能理清思绪。展现自己幽默的一面，把生活中的困境看作可以拿来打趣的障碍，而非压垮自己的重担，或许能让你更轻松地度过难关。

sentences.english: And who knows, you may just discover a talent for writing at the end of it.
sentences.chinese: 谁知道呢，说不定最后你还能发掘出自己的写作天赋呢。
